title: Final setup and cable
caption: I made the hole for the cable with the soldering iron. Not elegant but you can’t see it.

title: What cable!?
caption: I really like how the cable turned out. Nice and hidden.

title: Almost done the first time
caption: I thought it was done! But 4 magnets just weren’t strong enough. I could bump the touchstone off or take the whole thing off when removing the phone.

title: Final setup
caption: This is the final setup with 8 magnets set higher. The holder arms are adjustable.

title: Rotates
caption: It even rotates! This was kind of an after thought but I use nDrive beta on my Pre3 and it looks a lot better in landscape.

title: Add-A-Fuse
caption: Here’s my add-a-fuse and circuit breaker in my car. Pretty simple.

title: 8 Magnets on the Holder
caption: I actually removed the first 4 magnets and moved all of them up to give the Pre3 more room. The bottom of the Pre3 and Pixi rest ever so slightly onto the two extension feet of the holder.

title: First full Setup
caption: You can’t tell but this is the first complete setup with 4 magnets. They were too low and didn’t give the Pre3 enough room. Looked good though without the Pre3 on it!

title: My View
caption: It clears my turn signal easily by 2-3 inches. I can see it clearly but it’s not distracting.

title: Finished Product
caption: Sporting my Pre2 the day I was done with the project. Looks great!

title: Ground
caption: A look at the final ground setup.

title: TS Bottom
caption: Here you can see the cut I made pretty well. This cleared out room for the angled cable. It’s an early attempt with only 4 magnets.

title: In sunlight
caption: With the holder so close to the window it was important to see how it would look in direct sunlight. I think it’s doing great.

title: Angled Cable
caption: An early look at the setup where you can see only 4 magnets on the holder. Angled cable ready to go.

title: TS Back
caption: Here’s an early look at the back. Still has 4 magnets but I’d made the cut to fit the cable already.

I think it turned out pretty great!
The top layer with everything inside.
Trying to get those years old curves out was near impossible! Two part glue helped.
Gluing the case was the most difficult part.

title: 7a
caption: Wahlah! The top and bottom are almost done.
Cut the cardboard layer and I traced these phones into position.

title: 9a
caption: The day after I finished, my son pulled it off a shelf splitting this corner. This is my fix for it.
This was tedious. If I had to do it over I would layer cardboard and dremel it out!
I added a separate layer for the bottom and use bubble wrap for added cushion.
Starting to get the bottom covered in felt.
Early magnet layout and top layer design.
The revised magnets in the top layer. Finished the tablet felt.
How it looks closed. I think it retains the character of the original beat up guitar case.
You can see the pop riveted hinges. The hinges are the same ones from the bass case. I tried to use everything I could from the original.
How it looks when you open the case.
The top layer finished and out of the case. You can see the pull tabs I added on the left and right to pull it out of the case.
You can see the cut up shoe string I used for pull tabs to get the phones out.
Finished bottom layer in the case.
An early thought on the phones I would use.
Getting a rectangle from that shape was trying. Printer paper helped.
